components.text: Print books per adult in 2022: urban 5.61, rural 3.77.

items.label: Books read per child a year
items.note: Children's and adults' books are counted differently, so compare only the rates

footnote: Source: 15th, 17th to 20th and 23rd National Reading Surveys
notes: Who reads less? The urban-rural gap is steady. In 2022 the book reading rate was 68.6% for urban adults and 50.2% for rural adults, a gap of 18.4 points that barely narrowed in five years. Urban adults read 5.61 print books a year, rural adults 3.77. These are the latest urban-rural figures in any public release. Releases since 2023 say only that cities read more, with no numbers. At the other end are children: 86.7% of those aged 0 to 17 read books, 11.72 a year on average, with 36.82 minutes of print reading a day, all well above adults. The ones reading less are adults, rural adults most of all. Recent releases give no adult reading rates by age or education.
